name: David A. Varderpool
fact: The 1994 Talisman prints a Sigma Nu sophomore from Danville called Dave Vanderpool at p. 70, and Vanderpool, Dave, 70 is the only entry of anything like that surname in the index of either digitised volume. Varderpool is not a surname; Vanderpool is, and r for n is the commonest scanning slip there is. This is very probably the same man, but one letter is not a proof, so no portrait has been filed. His cell is the fourth of the third row on p. 70, counting the fifteen names down the left column five to a row, and it is staged unfiled as _unmatched-1994-95-dave-vanderpool.jpg.

name: Edward "Eddie" Myers
fact: NO USABLE FACE. The 1993 Talisman index reads "Myers, Edward 204" and that is his only appearance in either digitised volume (the 1994 volume names no Myers at all). Page 204 is the Student Government Association group photograph. It cannot be read positionally. The caption prints rows of six, eight and seven, twenty-one people; the printed FIRST row of six resolves perfectly, the figures running man, woman, man, woman, man, woman exactly as Donnie Miller, Jennifer Raffaelli, Jeremy Sublett, Susan Mitchell, Joe Rains, Cindy Hayes do. The other two rows do not. The group stands staggered on risers in four or five height bands rather than three, the topmost band holds eight figures where the printed third row has seven, and two of those eight are women where the third row's names are six men and Kibby Rose. An older grey-haired man stands in the middle of the top band who is very likely a faculty adviser and is not in the caption at all. Myers is first in the printed third row, so a mis-set row costs the identification outright. Two earlier researchers measured this same photograph independently and both put the faces at about eighteen pixels; measured again at native resolution here, the page is 864 pixels wide, the photograph 388 pixels wide, and a face runs about thirty pixels. No crop was cut.

name: Amy Braden
fact: A FRAME EXISTS AND IS REFUSED. Five names, five women, and the caption gives no positions, so there is no sex or order test to run: it identifies nobody. The frame itself would fail anyway. It is a low-angle theatrical shot in which one figure in a white robe fills most of the picture with her head thrown back and her mouth open, and the others are behind her with hands over their faces or in deep shadow. A Florence freshman in February 1996 would be a sophomore in 1996-97, which fits the officer, but that is the only thing that does.

name: Steven Graham
fact: A FRAME EXISTS, IS CORRECTLY LABELLED, AND HAS NO FACE IN IT. The Herald's People Poll of 12 September 1996, p. 4, runs five mugshots in a row, each with its quotation and then its name set in bold directly beneath its own frame, and the leftmost reads "Steven Graham, Guthrie freshman". The identification of the FRAME is therefore sound. Two things stop it. First, the halftone is crushed: measured at the scan's native resolution the face is 52 per cent of pixels below tone 60, the whole head reads as one black shape and the only feature that survives is the line of the teeth; a level stretch between the 1st and 60th percentiles recovers nothing, exactly as with the refused Anne Guillory frame. Second, the PERSON is not proved. Nothing in the caption ties this student to student government; all the archive has is a Guthrie freshman of that name in the same academic year as a Steven Graham who answered a roll call on 3 December 1996. Recorded rather than filed so that a later pass with a better scan can weigh it.

name: Steve Roadcap
fact: THE MOST HEAVILY QUOTED MAN ON THIS BLOCK AND THERE IS NO PICTURE OF HIM. Thirty-seven separate passages in the digitised Herald of 1993-1996 and thirteen more in 1997-1998, from his first appearance as "Louisville freshman Steve Roadcap" on 8 December 1994, through Campus Improvements chairman in 1995-96, unopposed candidate for treasurer in March 1996, treasurer through 1996-97 (the cable-television plan of 16 January 1997, the Provide-A-Ride shuttle of 23 January 1997, the memorial trees of 8 April 1997), a defeated run for treasurer again in April 1997 (Chad Lewis 518, Roadcap 327), and judicial foreman in 1997-98. This is the clearest single case on the block of the pattern the archive has measured elsewhere: the Herald quotes SGA officers constantly and photographs almost none of them.

src.label: College Heights Herald 72:4, 29 August 1996, printed p. 6

name: Kara Wallace
fact: A FRAME EXISTS, IT NAMES HER ALONE, AND THE SCAN HAS NO FACE IN IT. The Herald of 28 March 1996, printed p. 9, leads its Womens History Month page with a photograph by Kurt Fattic captioned "Tapping to Ms. Otis Regrets, Somerset freshman Kara Wallace performed in McCormack Hall on Tuesday night during the Womens History Forum", and the same page carries a pull quote signed Kara Wallace, Somerset freshman. The caption names one person, so the identification would be sound. It cannot be used: the frame is a stage photograph shot against a dark ground and in this scan it has printed as an almost solid black rectangle, with no face recoverable at any magnification. Checked at native resolution, 1272 pixels to the page. That single item is her only appearance in all 262 digitised Heralds of 1993-1996; she is otherwise in the archive from the SGA record of 29 October 1996 alone. Absent from the 1993 and 1994 Talisman indexes.

src.label: College Heights Herald 71:48, 28 March 1996, printed p. 9

name: Kristin Willis
fact: A FRAME EXISTS, THE POSITION IS GIVEN, AND IT IS REFUSED ON JUDGEMENT. The Herald of 27 April 1995, printed p. 2, runs a Craig Allen photograph captioned "In memory: During a candlelight vigil last night in the Valley, Amy Steinkamp (left), a junior from Chandler, Ind., and Louisville freshman Kristin Willis mourn for victims in the Oklahoma City bombing." Two women are in the frame and the caption positions one of them, so the other is Willis, and her face is large, lit by the candle and legible on a page scanned 2106 pixels across. It is refused because of what it shows: she is weeping with her eyes shut and her mouth open at a memorial for the dead. The archive wants the most flattering picture of a person, and a grieving face at a vigil is not one; it is the same class of frame as an arrest or a censure. Recorded rather than buried so that a later pass does not spend a run rediscovering it. Her only other appearance in the 1993-1996 Herald is a text mention. If nothing better is ever found and the editor wants it, the frame is at that citation and Willis is the figure on the right.

src.label: College Heights Herald 70:56, 27 April 1995, printed p. 2

name: Sarah Flynn
fact: A FRAME EXISTS AND HAS NO USABLE FACE. The Herald of 14 November 1995, printed p. 2, runs a Kurt Fattic photograph captioned "King of the Hill: The title of Mr. Hilltopper goes to Doug Evans, a senior from Ocala, Fla., and captain of the Western swim team ... He is cheered on by Sarah Flynn, a freshman from Gallatin, Tenn., and member of Alpha Delta Pi." Two people are named, and the man in the crown and dinner jacket at centre right is unmistakably Evans, so Flynn should be the woman cheering at the left. Two things stop it. The caption gives her no position, so the crowd behind them is not excluded; and at native resolution her head is thrown back with her own raised arm across her face, her eyes are lost in shadow and only an open mouth and a cheekbone are legible. Nothing cuttable. That is her only appearance in all 262 digitised Heralds of 1993-1996. Absent from the 1993 and 1994 Talisman indexes, whose only Flynns are Rebecca in 1993 and Leslie in 1994.

src.label: College Heights Herald 71:23, 14 November 1995, printed p. 2

name: Stephanie Greenwell
fact: A FRAME EXISTS, IT IS CORRECTLY IDENTIFIED, AND IT HAS NO FACE IN IT. The Heralds Greek Week photo spread of 11 April 1995, printed p. 11, carries a caption block that describes two photographs at once: "Above, Brad Bartz, a senior from Evansville, Ind., coaches the Chi Omega team ... Right, Owensboro senior Stephanie Greenwell helps her Alpha Gamma Delta sisters prepare for the three-legged race last Thursday afternoon." The Right photograph is the Scott Panella frame beside the caption block, and it is a tight shot of four pairs of legs and a pair of hands tying an ankle strap. No head appears in it at all. Checked at native resolution, 2894 pixels across. Her only other appearances in the 1993-1996 Herald are as a name in the SGA vacancy story of 13 January 1994 and in deans list advertisements. The 1993 Talisman index has Greenwell, Kimberly and the 1994 index Greenwell, Kim, both a different person.

src.label: College Heights Herald 70:51, 11 April 1995, printed p. 11

name: Michelle Kustes
fact: TWO FRAMES EXIST, BOTH NAME HER, AND NEITHER SHOWS HER FACE. The Heralds Trail Mix photo page of 4 April 1995, printed p. 7, is a picture story about an Outdoor Recreation class canoeing the Nolin River and names her twice. The large centre photograph is captioned "Nashville senior Stephanie Loughran (left) and Kustes relax while waiting for class members to start down the Nolin River", which positions Loughran and therefore fixes Kustes as the other figure; both women lie in the canoe with their heads down and turned away, and at native resolution, 2168 pixels to the page, neither face is present. The small photograph at the head of the page is captioned "While fishing with a make-shift pole on the Nolin River, Paris senior Phillip Humphrey laughs with Louisville senior Michelle Kustes"; two figures appear, a standing man with a rod and a seated woman, so the sexes separate them, but she is perhaps twenty-five pixels of shadowed profile. Nothing cuttable from either. An earlier pass had already written her off as absent from the 1991-1994 Talisman indexes; she is, and this is why she has no portrait.

src.label: College Heights Herald 70:49, 4 April 1995, printed p. 7

name: Melani Fischer
fact: A FRAME NAMES HER AND CANNOT IDENTIFY HER. Mitchell freshman Megan Monohan while Evansville sophomore Melani Fischer AND OTHERS cheer after the Kappa Delta victory. Absent from the 1993 and 1994 Talisman indexes, whose only Fischer is Brandi in 1994.

name: Drew Harrell
fact: SEAT RECOVERED. The archive records him for 1996-97 only as a Congress member with the seat not stated, from a roll call. src.label: College Heights Herald 72:31, 23 January 1997, printed p. 3

name: Steven Graham
fact: THE EARLIER REFUSAL IS CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY, AND A SECOND FRAME IS NOW KNOWN AND IS NO BETTER. Re-rendered from the scan at native resolution on this run: the People Poll frame of 12 September 1996, printed p. 4, leftmost of five, labelled Steven Graham, Guthrie freshman, prints as a solid black silhouette in which the only feature that survives is the line of the teeth. Nothing is recoverable. A SECOND label of the same name and home town exists and had not been found before, in the Herald of 9 December 1997, printed p. 4, reading Steven Graham, Guthrie sophomore, which confirms the class progression from the 1996 frame and confirms there is one such student, not two. It is another People Poll frame in the same style and it does not solve the picture problem. Both stand refused on the frame, and the person remains unproved in either case: nothing in either caption ties this student to student government, and all the archive has is a name answering a roll call on 3 December 1996.

src.label: College Heights Herald 72:7, 12 September 1996, p. 4; and 73:24, 9 December 1997, p. 4

name: ALL 39 OFFICERS OF THE n9396 BLOCK
fact: OFFICER AUDIT, 5 SEPTEMBER 2026. STATE: 10 of the 39 officers now have a face and the other 29 each have a written reason in this file. The eight found before this run are Ernie Chen, Jason Young, Jeffery L. Yan, Jeff Yan, Shawna Whartenby, Amy France, Laura Hancock and Travis Mayo. Two were added on this run, TROY A. NUNN and DREW HARRELL, both by overturning or extending an earlier refusal rather than by finding a new source. WHAT WAS RUN AGAINST THE 39 ON THIS PASS, all of it exhaustive rather than sampled: (1) every one of the 4,973 pages of the 262 digitised Heralds of 1993-1996 searched for each officer name and its spelling variants; (2) a mugshot-label index built over the whole corpus, 4,706 candidate labels, being every short run that parses as a personal name with a class or home-town line beside it, matched against all 39; (3) a photo-credit proximity sweep, every occurrence of an officer name within twelve runs of a photographer credit; (4) every page carrying both an SGA headline and a photographer credit, 65 of them, read one by one; (5) the same label and proximity sweeps over the 1997, 1998 and 1999 Heralds for the officers who were still students then; (6) a COMPLETE People Poll roster, 316 poll pages across 1993-1999 yielding 2,522 distinct printed names, matched against all 39 officers and all 133 worklist names. WHAT THAT PROVES: the People Poll, which gave five of this blocks eleven new faces, is now exhausted. There is no unexamined mugshot of any of the 29 in the digitised Herald of 1993-1999. THREE REFUSALS RE-TESTED AGAINST THE PAGE IMAGE ON THIS RUN AND TWO CONFIRMED: Steven Grahams People Poll frame of 12 September 1996 is a black silhouette with only the teeth legible, refusal stands, and a second frame of him of 9 December 1997 was found and is no better; Anne Guillorys frame of 2 May 1996 is a backlit silhouette with her hand across her mouth, refusal stands; Troy A. Nunns frame of 12 March 1996 was refused as a face turned away and it is not, it is a lit three-quarter view, so it is now published. THE PATTERN, measured rather than asserted: the Herald of these years quotes SGA officers constantly and photographs almost none of them. Steve Roadcap is the extreme case at fifty separate passages and no picture. Officers reach print as pull quotes, letter signatures and roll-call names, all of which this run separated out and none of which carries a frame.

name: Andy Gailor
fact: SPELLING, AND A PROBABLE DUPLICATE THE ARCHIVE SHOULD LOOK AT. The worklist for this block carries ANDREW GAILER as a Junior Off-Campus Representative in 1995-96 and the officers list carries ANDY GAILOR as Legislative Research chairman in 1996-97 and 1997-98. They are almost certainly one man. The Herald of 16 January 1997, printed p. 6, attributes a pull quote to "Andy Gailor, Louisville senior", and a Louisville senior in 1996-97 was a junior in 1995-96, which is exactly the seat and year recorded for Gailer. The deans list of 22 February 1994 gives the full form "Andrew King Gailor". There is no Gailer of any given name anywhere in the 262 digitised Heralds of 1993-1996; the surname simply does not occur. Flagged, not merged, per the archives rule. NO PHOTOGRAPH either way: the 16 January 1997 item is a pull-quote box of type only, and the one story about him, the rental-deposit feature of 16 October 1997, printed p. 1, runs its photographs of other people and shows him not at all.

name: Jessica Merman
fact: ONE NEAR MISS, WORTH RECORDING SO IT IS NOT RE-CHECKED. fact: SPIRIT MASTERS CHAIRMAN 1994-95, AND THAT ROUTE IS CLOSED. src.label: College Heights Herald 70:9, 22 September 1994, printed p. 13

name: XPOSURE MAGAZINES 1995-1996 - ROUTE OPENED AND CLOSED
fact: SOURCE OPENED FOR THE FIRST TIME AND SPENT. Xposure is what replaced the Talisman yearbook when it stopped, and it covers exactly the years this block has no yearbook for, so it looked like the one unworked source left. It is not. Three issues are digitised, TopSCHOLAR dlsc_ua_records articles 1422 (fall 1995), 1423 (spring 1996) and 1424 (summer 1996), 132 pages in all, and they have no usable embedded text layer, only the cover sheet. All 132 pages were rendered and OCR'd with Apple Vision on this run and the output is kept at ~/Desktop/SGA60 photo hunt/_xposure-ocr-1995-1996/ with a README. WHAT IT PROVES: there are no portrait grids and no index of people, and of the 172 people on this blocks officer and worklist files exactly ONE is named anywhere in the three issues. That is Kristin Willis, quoted as a Louisville sophomore in a feature on prayer and healing at fall 1995 printed pp. 20-21; the single photograph on that spread is of somebody else and is captioned so. Every other apparent match is a common surname belonging to a different person. Native scan resolution is about 780 pixels to a printed page, below even the 1990s Talismans, so a face found here would have been marginal anyway. Do not re-open this.
